title: JClaw eval suite
description: A set of eval cases. One suite per file, named <id>.json. Edit suites in place — git holds the history, and each run records a content fingerprint so two runs scored by different suite content are never compared silently. JCLAW-875, JCLAW-883.

id.description: Suite identifier. Must match the filename.
Case identifier, unique within the suite. Reports and regression comparisons key on it, so renaming a case discards its history.

input.description: The user turn sent to the agent.

rubric.description: One line stating what this case is testing and why it earns its place in the suite.

kind.description: Every kind is decidable without a model call. Model-judged checks land with the critic (JCLAW-836).

args.description: contains_all / not_contains_any: the substrings (case-insensitive). matches: one regex. tools_called_exactly: the complete set of tool names the turn may call, compared as a multiset — an empty array asserts no tool at all. tools_called_within: the tools the turn MAY call, none of them required — the 'or' form, for when a tool is optional because the harness already supplied what it would return. Tool assertions are allowlists on purpose: a denylist only catches rogue calls someone predicted. Per-kind arity is enforced by EvalDatasetLoader; only tools_called_exactly permits an empty array.

schema.description: json_schema only: the schema the response must satisfy. EvalScorer implements a documented subset — type, properties, required, items, enum, additionalProperties, description — and the loader rejects any other keyword rather than ignoring it.

limit.description: max_llm_calls only: the call budget for the case (JCLAW-833's efficiency NFR, measured via llm_call_count from JCLAW-882).
